While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, there are always specific, less predictable events that could push the actual results beyond these bands. On the upside, an unanticipated surge in demand, a breakthrough innovation, surprisingly strong economic data, or a significant positive policy announcement could lead to the metric exceeding the upper bounds of our intervals. Conversely, outcomes could fall below the lower bounds due to sudden negative economic shocks, unforeseen regulatory changes, geopolitical instability, or other "black swan" events that fundamentally alter the landscape and were not fully factored into our initial probabilistic assessment.
